dossier.public_summary: The light curve shows clear odd-even differences, a strong secondary eclipse about a third as deep as the primary, and depths that swing from zero to over 1500 ppm. This pattern is typical of a blended eclipsing binary folded at half its true period, not a single planet transiting the bright K dwarf. No centroid image confirms the dip is on the target, so contamination remains possible, but the on-target binary signal alone is a planet false positive.

reasons.why: Coherent difference between odd and even transits seen in every sector (sector_oe_max_sigma 12.77, sectors_over_3 4, same_sign_share 0.4444) – expected for eclipsing binary at twice the period.
reasons.value: 5.967 (odd 144 ppm vs even 299.2 ppm, depth_ratio 2.1, PPD 0.5186)

reasons.why: Real second dip well above brightening and stellar companion's occultation, not a hot-planet phase curve; sector_sec_half_max_snr 4.202 with sectors_over_3 1 and positive_share 0.2222.
reasons.value: 9.673 at phase 0.6129, depth_ppm 77.75, depth_over_dip 0.3289, best_brightening_snr 6.27, secondary_over_bump 1.543

reasons.why: Depth unstable even within one source and driven by a few very deep events, inconsistent with a planet.
reasons.value: p_consistent 1.218848697949924e-298, chi2 1478.1 dof 23, share_of_top_3 0.767, outliers at 1512 ppm (23.5 sigma, 2514 ppm 16 sigma, 1036 ppm 13.3 sigma)

reasons.why: Depth changes much more than photometric calibration can explain; not a stable planetary transit even without the few deep outliers.
reasons.value: 3.297e-57, depth_change_pct 433.1; sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source, SPOC 2-min p_constant 5.537404046077863e-59

reasons.why: No difference image to place the dip on-target, so a neighbour within 1 pixel that could cause the dip with ~14% eclipse at 15.5 arcsec cannot be ruled out; combined with binary indicators this favours a false positive/blend over a planet.
reasons.value: inconclusive (diff_snr -1.771 sector 68, -0.6824 sector 104; centroid_all also inconclusive)
